comment: Student plan is now $5.99 and I'm a broke sophomore, so that's rough. Still cheaper than a Netflix sub though, so I'm staying for now.
Lol $1 more on Individual, I've been paying $9.99 since 2016. Inflation is inflation, I'll stay.
Spotify is greedy af, they had record profits last quarter and now they want more from us. Cancelled and moved to Apple Music.
Family plan going to $16.99 is fine for us, five people so it's split. Still the best deal in music.
Artists are the ones who never see this money. Price goes up, royalties stay at like half a cent per stream. Where's the artist pay increase?
Duo going up $2 for a couple who already splits a bill, meh. We're dropping to the individual plan and they can pay their own share.
Still no lossless after two years of promises and now the price goes up? Not paying more for the same 320kbps. I'm gone.
Price bump is basically nothing, it's like one coffee a month. Music is worth it.
I'm mostly listening to Rogan and audiobooks now, so honestly the music price is the least of my worries. Whatever.
Every streaming service raised prices this year, so Spotify is just catching up. Expected.
YouTube Music Premium is $10.99 and gives you background play plus all of YouTube. Spotify just pushed me to switch.
Going back to the free tier honestly. Ads every few songs are annoying but I'm not paying $11 for podcasts I don't listen to.
Spotify keeps tweaking the app with the new UI and now they want more money. The app is getting worse, not better.
Piracy has never looked so good. I'm not paying a dollar more for a service that still doesn't have lossless, I'll just download stuff.
Haven't gotten my email about the price change on my existing plan yet. Anyway it's a fair increase for what you get.
Apple Music is $10.99 too and I already have it bundled with my iCloud storage. Thinking about moving over.
Tidal costs more, so Spotify is still the cheapest option that doesn't suck. Keeping it.
Student discount going from $4.99 to $5.99 is a 20 percent hike for students. That's just mean.
Spotify says this helps artists but we all know where the money goes. Executives get paid first, every time.
It's the first US price increase in about 12 years, that's pretty reasonable. Happy to pay.
Dropping from Duo to individual because we're splitting the bill differently now. The price is not the main reason, but it doesn't help.
I'm moving to Amazon Music since I'm already paying for Prime. The price increase is just the nail in the coffin.
I don't really use Spotify much anymore, just for the occasional playlist. The price doesn't matter to me.
The price keeps going up and the features keep getting removed. I'm done.
Spotify is a great service and a dollar more a month is nothing. Keep up the good work.
Price bumps are annoying but let's be real, $10.99 for ad-free music is still good. I'd only leave if the library gets worse.
